title: Distributed In-Memory Cache
summary: Build a horizontally scalable key-value cache shared by many services.
statement:
Design a distributed in-memory cache cluster used by many application services to speed up reads.

Functional requirements:
- `get`, `set` with a time-to-live, and `delete` operations on string keys and byte values.
- Memory is bounded; the cache evicts entries when full.
- Nodes can be added or removed without remapping most keys.
- Losing one node must not take the whole cache down.

Scale to assume:
- 10 TB of cached data in total.
- 5 million operations per second at peak.
- Sub-millisecond latency for most operations within a data center.
hints: How does a client decide which node owns a key, and what happens to that decision when a node joins?
Pick an eviction policy and the data structure that makes it constant time per operation.
A single very popular key can overload one node. What would you do about it?
expectations: Clarifies consistency expectations, value sizes, persistence (none or optional), and whether the cache is look-aside or read-through.
Sizes the cluster from total memory and per-node throughput, including replication overhead.
Partitions keys with consistent hashing and virtual nodes, with routing in a client library or proxy.
Uses LRU or a similar eviction policy implemented with a hash map plus linked list, and lazy plus periodic TTL expiry.
Replicates to followers for availability and discusses failover and the consistency tradeoffs of asynchronous replication.
Mitigates hot keys with replication or client-side local caching and prevents stampedes with request coalescing or jittered TTLs.
Discusses cache invalidation strategies with the backing database and the risk of stale reads.
